preregistration: D-381 (the author's step-4 item 1, 2026-10-07); details by the closest D-entries (D-181): D-152 4c, D-241, D-248, D-255, D-264, D-278, D-156, D-164, D-177 (b)

input_verification.rule: D-170/D-172: a result with a flag enters no paper table until D-168 has passed

ks.statistic: two-sample KS D (max |ECDF difference|, exact counts), cal_d pre vs post, per seed; score = mean over seeds
ks.flag: mean D > critical value, one flag per draw for every class
ks.text: D-381 (2)(a): the two-sample KS test (arXiv:1810.11953, BBSDs + KS) on the probe score of cal_d, pre against post, per seed; the flag is the mean of D over seeds > 1.358 sqrt((n + m) / (n m)) (alpha 0.05, asymptotic). Stated, not corrected: the two samples are the same prompts, which the test's independence premise does not cover; it is applied as a deployer would apply it.

atc.confidence: max(p, 1 - p), p = sigmoid(s - T_d); counted in margin space |s - T_d|
atc.fit_set: cal_d negatives + threshold_calib positives, pre model
atc.threshold: the (k+1)-th smallest labelled margin, k = pre errors at T_d
atc.estimate: share of cal_d below t under a model, floored at 1/n_cal
atc.ratio: post / pre per seed, mean over seeds

bbse.text: D-381 (2)(c) as amended by D-392 (1): BBSE (arXiv:1802.03916) is computed BESIDE as a ranking line, with no flag (no registered cut), and does not enter P-C5.3. Per cell, draw and seed the estimated harmful share on the benign reference w = (r_post - r_pre) / (TPR_pre - r_pre): r the share of cal_d at or above T_d under a model, floored at 1/n (4c's direct ratio's r); TPR_pre the share of the calibration positives at or above T_d under the pre model, unfloored; undefined when TPR_pre <= r_pre (counted); the cell's value is the mean over the seeds with a defined estimate, and a cell with none is left out of that draw's ROC AUC (counted per row); ROC score |w|. Within one cell, draw and seed (r_pre, TPR_pre fixed) w is an increasing affine function of r_post, and w >= w_c if and only if r_post / r_pre >= 1 + w_c (TPR_pre - r_pre) / r_pre; across a row's cells it is not a function of the direct ratio (TPR_pre differs by cell, the direct ratio is a mean over seeds), so its ranking can differ. Its premise, p(x | y) unchanged across the shift, is what a backbone update breaks: the scores of both classes move.
bbse.premise: p(x | y) unchanged: broken by an update (D-392 (1))

anchor.rule: every per-draw array of healthcheck_d156's six statistics, per layer, probe set and level, equals the 4c npz byte for byte; with every layer, the Gaussian and direct counts summed over cells too

draws_npz.keys: L<layer>|<probe set>|<level>|<array> for the arrays ks_mean_D, atc_ratio, atc_est_pre, atc_est_post, atc_error_rate_pre, bbse_harmful_share, bbse_tpr_pre, bbse_n_undefined_seeds and realised_paired_ratio (and, LoRA at 5% only, healthcheck_d156's z_mean, log_sd_ratio, gaussian_ratio, log_gaussian_ratio, direct_ratio); counts|<probe set>|<level>|<detector>|<class>|tp/fn/fp/tn for the detectors ks, atc, gaussian, direct, summed over the cells; index 0 the frozen split, then the draws
